info.title: KISS API Reference
info.description: This reference covers the endpoints most integrations use. Need an endpoint that is not here? Contact your KISS rep.

get.description: Everything the signed-in user's app needs to operate offline: their units with the evaluated access state, the entry points for their zones, the NFC keys, and the facility timezone. Authenticated with the user's Bearer token. Cache it and refresh on launch / pull-to-refresh.
Liveness probe. Returns `200` when the API is up.

post.description: Record a lock event (open or close: success, failure, or blocked) after an NFC interaction.
Record an entry-point event (gate or door) after an NFC interaction.

parameters.name: filter[phone_number]
parameters.description: Substring match against the stored country code + number.

parameters.name: filter[location]
parameters.description: Only tenants homed at this location, addressed by its KISS `location_id` (ULID).

parameters.name: filter[external_location_code]
parameters.description: Only tenants at the location with this code in your own system. Company-token callers only.

parameters.name: filter[external_tenant_id]
parameters.description: Look up specific tenants by the id they carry in your own system. Company-token callers only.

parameters.name: filter[type]
parameters.description: Narrow to `primary`, `secondary-tenant`, or `unit-accessor`. Same vocabulary as the `type` field on each row.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page to return. Paging details come back in `meta.pagination`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 15, capped at 100.

200.description: A page of tenants, in the shape that matches your token. A company token gets the tenants at its locations, each carrying both ids plus `phone_number`, so a tenant with no `external_tenant_id` can still be matched against your own records. A staff token gets the manager shape instead. Send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match` on the next sweep to skip pages that have not changed.

304.description: Your `If-None-Match` matched: this page has not changed since that `ETag`, and no body is sent. Skip it and move on to the next page.

get.description: The tenants KISS already holds for your locations, so you can reconcile them against your own records before you write. Each row carries both ids: your own `external_tenant_id` and the KISS `tenant_id` (a ULID). Rows with a null `external_tenant_id` are tenants KISS knows that you have not claimed — someone who signed up in the app, walked in, or arrived through another integration. Match those on `phone_number` and reuse the existing person rather than pushing a new id for them, which is what keeps you from creating a duplicate. Results are paged (15 per page, `per_page` up to 100) with paging details in `meta.pagination`, and can be narrowed with `filter[location]`, `filter[external_location_code]`, or `filter[external_tenant_id]`. Supports conditional requests via `ETag` / `If-None-Match`, so a periodic sweep can skip pages that have not changed. Needs the `tenants:read` scope.

200.description: One tenant, addressed by its KISS `tenant_id` (ULID), in the shape that matches your token: a company token gets the reconciliation fields, a staff token the manager fields.

get.description: Fetch a single tenant by their KISS `tenant_id` (ULID). Returns `404` for a tenant outside the locations your token reaches. Needs the `tenants:read` scope.

parameters.name: filter[location]
parameters.description: Return only units at this location, addressed by its KISS `location_id` (ULID).

parameters.name: filter[external_location_code]
parameters.description: Return only units at the location with this code in your own system. Company-token callers only.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page to return. Paging details come back in `meta.pagination`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 15, capped at 100.

get.description: Lists the units in your company, each carrying both IDs: your own `external_unit_id` and the KISS `unit_id` (a ULID). This is the mapping to store if you want to address single units by ULID. Results are paged (15 per page, `per_page` up to 100) with paging details in `meta.pagination`, and can be narrowed to one store with `filter[location]` or `filter[external_location_code]`. Supports conditional requests via `ETag` / `If-None-Match`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique request identifier for deduplication (1–255 chars, 24 h window)

200.description: Sync applied. `results` maps every applied item to its KISS `unit_id`; anything that failed is in `errors` instead.

422.description: Every item in the batch failed. Same body as a 200; inspect `errors`.

patch.description: Create or update up to 500 units in one idempotent call, matched on your `external_unit_id`. Unknown IDs create units, known IDs update their facts. This is the only write keyed on your own IDs, so you can change any unit fact (occupancy, lockout, balance, auction, move-in) without storing KISS ULIDs; send a single-item `units` array to update one unit by `external_unit_id`. Use it for the initial roster load and periodic reconciliation. Every applied unit comes back in `data.results` with its KISS `unit_id`, so you can record the mapping without a second call. Per-item failures come back in `data.errors` with a `200`; a batch where every item failed answers `422` with the same body.

get.description: Fetch a single unit by its KISS `unit_id` (ULID).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique request identifier for deduplication (1–255 chars, 24 h window)

put.description: Addressed by the unit's KISS `unit_id` (ULID). Set the unit's single primary user (the owner). Marks the unit occupied, sets the move-in date, clears any lockout, and (with a `tenant` block) creates or updates that user so they can claim the unit in the app. If the unit already has a primary user, this REPLACES them — the prior primary link is overwritten (guest / secondary accessors are left attached). Adding a guest is a separate flow, not this endpoint.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique request identifier for deduplication (1–255 chars, 24 h window)

delete.description: Addressed by the unit's KISS `unit_id` (ULID). End the primary tenancy and reset the unit to vacant (no request body). Clears occupied, the primary-user link, pms_tenant_id, move_in_date, balance_due (to 0), paid_through_date, pms_lockout, pms_auction, pms_unrentable, and pms_status_raw, and detaches secondary accessors. Returns 404 for an unknown unit.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique request identifier for deduplication (1–255 chars, 24 h window)

patch.description: Sparse update of one unit's access facts (overlock, exemption, auction, unrentable, balance, occupancy). Addressed by the KISS `unit_id` (ULID), so reach for it when you already hold the ULID (from `GET /units`). To update by your own `crm_unit_id` instead, send a one-item batch to `PATCH /units`. Send only the fields that changed.

key.description:
Only the device open/close actions a client reports. Server-generated
keys (registration, bundle, access-share) are written by their own
flows and must not be forgeable through this endpoint.

reason.description:
KEEP-1277: `nullable` is REQUIRED here, not cosmetic. `reason` is
optional for every key except the two failure keys above, but the
global ConvertEmptyStringsToNull middleware rewrites an empty string
to null, and without `nullable` a null value then fails the `string`
rule and 422s the whole request.

error_code.description:
KEEP-1150: telemetry must never fail the whole request. An error
code the server does not recognise is coerced to null in the
controller (AccessLogErrorCode::tryFrom), so validating it with
Rule::in only served to 422 the primary open/close outcome log and
drop it entirely. Accept any string; the model's enum cast + the
controller tryFrom still guarantee only valid values or null persist.

field_lost_after_start.description: KEEP-1148: flags a real open the phone was pulled away from mid-motor.

package.description:
KEEP-1154: which NFC engine + version produced the tap (kiss_core /
tapt_nfc + its version), so performance can be sliced by NFC stack
across apps and the bench.

ClaimLockRequest.description:
Validates a consumer NFC lock claim (KEEP-805).

`serial_number` is the lock's printed/encoded serial — the value an NFC tap
surfaces. KISS locks identify themselves by serial number everywhere a
physical scan resolves a device (see the B2B chip lookup in
{@see IndexController}, which resolves a
tapped serial via `Lock::whereSerialNumber()`), so the consumer claim accepts
the same field rather than inventing a new payload format.

Authorization is handled by the `consumer.scope` route middleware
(KEEP-802), so this request only validates shape.
ClaimLockRequest.title: ClaimLockRequest

ConfirmPhoneChangeRequest.description:
Validates the OTP confirming a consumer phone change (KEEP-962).
Authorization is handled by the `consumer.scope` route middleware.
ConfirmPhoneChangeRequest.title: ConfirmPhoneChangeRequest

GrantRole.description: Role on a grant. Owner = the one person who holds the subject (primary tenant in storage, consumer in POS); Guest = anyone else granted access. Zone grants have no role column — they are guest-only by construction — so this enum applies to unit and consumer grants only.
GrantRole.title: GrantRole

GrantScope.description: Scope on a grant. Inherited = the guest mirrors the subject's tenant access (owner-state-aware); Direct = access depends only on grant validity, independent of tenant state. Zone grants have no scope column — they are direct-only by construction — so this enum applies to unit and consumer grants only.
GrantScope.title: GrantScope

lockout.description: Whether the external system has the unit locked out (e.g. for delinquency).

lock_exempt.description: Whether the unit is exempt from lockout enforcement.

auction.description: Whether the unit is in auction status.

status_raw.description: The unit's raw status string in the external system.

occupied.description: Prohibited here — tenancy changes go through PUT/DELETE /units/{ulid}/tenancy.

tenant_id.description: Prohibited here — tenancy changes go through PUT/DELETE /units/{ulid}/tenancy.

external_tenant_id.description: Prohibited here — tenancy changes go through PUT/DELETE /units/{ulid}/tenancy.

pms_tenant_id.description: Legacy alias of `external_tenant_id`. Prohibited here — tenancy changes go through PUT/DELETE /units/{ulid}/tenancy.

move_in_date.description: Prohibited here — tenancy changes go through PUT/DELETE /units/{ulid}/tenancy.

PmsPushUnitGrantsRequest.description:
Authorizes + validates a PMS-partner push of a unit's grants (KEEP-758): the
machine-token write path that converges PMS sources onto access_grants.

A PMS token (Passport, pms:write) may push role=owner and role=guest+
scope=inherited; scope=direct — and any non-PMS caller — is a 403 (reusing the
shared {@see GrantRequest} caller matrix). The unit's owner + guest grants
arrive together in one `grants[]` payload. share_id is server-generated.

grantee_user_id.description:
The user ULID is canonical (KEEP-1155; integers are the internal
ids and stay accepted as a legacy alias). Either way the grantee is
scoped to the token's company: a connector pushes its own company's
tenants (owner + inherited guests), so an identity from another
company must not resolve to a grant on this company's unit.

PmsPushUnitGrantsRequest.title: PmsPushUnitGrantsRequest

external_unit_id.description:
Your system's unit identifier. Only used to label the unit when this
call creates it; it never re-targets or re-labels an existing unit.

crm_unit_id.description: Legacy alias of `external_unit_id`. Also create-only: it never re-targets an existing unit.

external_location_code.description: The location's code in your system, an alternative to `location_id`.

external_tenant_id.description: The moving-in tenant's identifier in your system.

status_raw.description: The unit's raw status string in the external system.

lock_exempt.description: Whether the unit is exempt from lockout enforcement.

external_tenant_id.description: The tenant's identifier in your system.

ShareLockRequest.description:
Validates a consumer lock share (KEEP-807).

The grantee is identified by phone in the same `country_code` + `phone_number`
shape the consumer auth flow uses {@see SendPhoneOtpRequest},
so the app can reuse the number it already has on hand. `expires_at`, when
present, bounds the guest grant's validity.

Authorization (consumer-type token) is handled by the `consumer.scope` route
middleware (KEEP-802); resolving the *owned* bundle for the target lock and
the grantee's consumer account happens in the controller. So this request only
validates shape.

name.description:
The recipient's name for a first-time invite (used to greet them in
the welcome SMS and to label the pending share until they sign up).

ShareLockRequest.title: ShareLockRequest

StorePaymentRequest.description:
Validates a V2 pay request. `type` selects which charges are settled (the
write-side mirror of the 342 invoice-read `filter[type]`); `period` applies
only to advance-pay. Card fields mirror V1 exactly — the PMS is the processor.
StorePaymentRequest.title: StorePaymentRequest

StorePhoneChangeRequest.description:
Validates the candidate number for a consumer phone change (KEEP-962).
Authorization is handled by the `consumer.scope` route middleware.
StorePhoneChangeRequest.title: StorePhoneChangeRequest

email.description:
password grant (manager). No exists: rule — the controller returns a
generic invalid-credentials response so the endpoint can't be used to
enumerate which emails exist.

StoreZoneGrantRequest.description:
Authorizes and validates creation of a single zone grant (KEEP-757) — the
vendor / contractor flow.

Zone grants are guest-and-direct by construction (no role or scope column on
zone_grants), so the request accepts neither: `role` and `scope` are
`prohibited`, turning an owner-on-a-zone or inherited-on-a-zone attempt into a
422 rather than silently creating the wrong thing.

Authorization is the zone slice of the caller matrix:
 - Tenants have no zone-share rights (zones are the B2B vendor flow) → 403.
 - Consumers never manage grants → 403 (belt-and-suspenders behind reject.consumer).
 - Staff (employee / admin-manager / partner-admin / super-admin) may create,
   gated on access to the zone's location.
 - PMS Passport tokens never reach here — the zone routes are Sanctum-only.
StoreZoneGrantRequest.title: StoreZoneGrantRequest

external_unit_id.description: Your system's unit identifier, an alternative to `unit_id`. Creates the unit when unknown.

external_location_code.description: The location's code in your system, an alternative to `location_id`.

external_tenant_id.description: The unit's current tenant identifier in your system.

lockout.description: Whether the external system has the unit locked out (e.g. for delinquency).

lock_exempt.description: Whether the unit is exempt from lockout enforcement.

auction.description: Whether the unit is in auction status.

status_raw.description: The unit's raw status string in the external system.

UpdateLockRequest.description:
Validates a consumer lock rename (KEEP-806).

The only mutable field on a claimed lock is its `display_name`, which is
stored on the owning POS bundle (`bundles.display_name`). The bounds mirror
the optional name accepted at claim time in {@see ClaimLockRequest}, except
rename requires a value — a PATCH with no name has nothing to change.

Authorization (consumer-type token) is handled by the `consumer.scope`
route middleware (KEEP-802); resolving the *owned* bundle for the target
lock — the per-resource authz boundary — happens in the controller, which
404s when the consumer does not own the lock. So this request only validates
shape.
UpdateLockRequest.title: UpdateLockRequest

UpdateProfileRequest.description:
Validates a consumer self-update of their display name (KEEP-962). A PATCH, so
either field may be sent alone, but at least one must be present and non-empty.
Authorization is handled by the `consumer.scope` route middleware.
UpdateProfileRequest.title: UpdateProfileRequest
